newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake, Va., acts to stem $19 million deficit.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake, Va., acts to stem $19 million deficit.

text.p: Chesapeake, Va., City Manager John Pazour ordered a partial hiring freeze and halted spending on new projects in order to stem an estimated deficit of $19 million, Virginian-Pilot reported Thursday.
The action came as the city raised its estimate of the deficit from the previous $14 million, the newspaper said.
Pazour said hiring decisions would be made case by case. The city has 2,666 full-time positions, of which 144 are vacant, and 350 part-time positions, of wich 81 are vacant.

Pazour told the newspaper that the previous administration had failed to notify city officials that Chesapeake had a $5 million shortfall in each of the last two years, leading to a cumulative deficit of $19 million.
He said revenues were expected to drop by $5.1 million this year, and will continue to drop before possibly rebounding in 1999.
City officials are considering an array of fee and tax increases to offset the deficit, the newspaper said.
However, it quoted Pazour as saying that the city has adequate reserves and that its AA bond rating is not in danger.
